REVIEW-21 HANDLING:

- F1 (MEDIUM, blocking) FIXED. Each stored hold now carries the admin's user id in both stores: shared/heldWriteStore.ts keepHold(slot, adminId, hold) and loadHold(slot, adminId, parseBody); payment-sheet/heldRecordings.ts keepHeldRecording(adminId, held) and loadHeldRecordings(month, adminId). Restore returns only the signed-in admin's holds and removes any other entry it meets (loadHold: that slot; loadHeldRecordings: that month, and it restores nothing if the drop fails).

- F1 session start: shells/admin/adminRuntime.ts wraps login (cookieSignIn and nativeSignIn) and restore (cookieRestore and nativeRestore) so a returned principal calls dropOtherAdminsHolds + dropOtherAdminsRecordings (new exports, built on heldWriteStore.dropOtherAdminsKeys). An entry without a readable adminId is dropped too, because it can never be restored. The same admin signing in again keeps their holds. Restore was added beyond the brief (rule 15): a reload whose cookies now belong to an admin who signed in in another tab is the same case.

- Admin id source: useSession().principal.userId. useHeldWrite and useRecordingSheetRecorder now call useSession(); a null principal means no persistence (nothing restored, persisted false, recordings kept in memory only).

- F2 FIXED. held is the body without idempotencyKey (stable object), and submit is a no-op while a write is held (pending or unknown). Existing callers already lock submit then, so there is no visible change.
- F3 FIXED. A hold captures {slot, adminId} when it is created (at submit or restore); keep and release use the captured place, never the current persist.slot.
- F4, F5: recorded below, not fixed.

CORRECTION to b593cb9's body: the payment sheet's held recording carries no contact details, only the client userId, fundId, amount, date, reason and schedule link. Only create-client bodies carry a name, email and phone.
FOR fx-admin-values AND fx-admin-funds:

- F4 (LOW, record only): an unreadable stored entry is ignored silently. In heldWriteStore, the owner matches but parseBody or the key check fails; in heldRecordings, parseHeld fails. The form or row then opens idle with no sign that a write was held, so the admin may enter it again under a new key. Surface it instead: show that a held write could not be read and the record must be checked before re-entering it. Entries of another admin, or without a readable owner, are now dropped on purpose (F1); that is not F4.

- F5 (LOW, record only): holds have no expiry, but the server's idempotency receipt lasts 24 h (idempotencyTtlMs). After that, Check again with the held key is answered IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, which api/errors.ts:82 classifies as unknown, so Check again loops on "Not confirmed" with no way out but reset. Rule 6 says define expiry: store a heldAt with each hold and, past the receipt lifetime, stop offering Check again and tell the admin to check the record.
- Tests of forms that adopt persist must mock useSession with principal: { userId }. The existing mocks return no principal, so persistence is silently off in them.
- held is now safe to render (no key). submit is ignored while held, so keep the inputs and the submit button locked on pending or unknown, as the current callers do.

- Still open from the previous handoff: useRecordingSheetRecorder record() ignores keepHeldRecording's false (CA-27 class). Moved hooks that mint a key per call must take idempotencyKey in their variables. Key a persisted form by its slot (key={slot}), with the record identity in the slot. Use persisted: refuse close while held !== null && !persisted.

DOUBTFUL (STATIC, not fixed, outside F1): an in-memory hold (no reload) in tab 1 survives another tab's sign-out and a different admin's sign-in, because cookies are shared and tab 1's React principal does not change. A write sent from tab 1 probably fails CSRF (tab 1 still holds the old token in memory), but a 401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED leads to a cookie refresh that reads the new admin's CSRF and resends as them. Worth a check by whoever owns http.ts and the session code.

- PERSISTED FLAG (b593cb9): useHeldWrite also returns persisted: boolean. True only when a requested save succeeded (keepHold true) or the hold was restored from storage; false without persist, when sessionStorage is unavailable/full, and after done, rejection or reset. A form that lets a persisted held write close must refuse close while held !== null && !persisted.

- SIGN-OUT CLEAR (b593cb9): shared/heldWriteStore.ts exports clearHeldKeys(prefix) and clearHolds(); payment-sheet/heldRecordings.ts gains clearHeldRecordings() only (plus its import of clearHeldKeys). shells/admin/adminRuntime.ts wraps the admin token store so clear("admin") also calls clearHeldWrites() (both stores). That clear is the single choke point of every admin session end: runtime logout (sign-out button), SessionProvider.signedOut, and http.ts endSession on SESSION_INVALID (revoked) and on a failed refresh after AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED (expiry). Client app untouched (build:client output identical, 17 assets 948169 bytes).

- Tradeoff: a hold whose outcome is still unknown is forgotten at session end; the admin must check the record before re-entering it. Not cleared: restore() returning null (e.g. a reload after the refresh cookie expired), because cookieRestore and nativeRestore also return null on an unreachable server; the bodies then stay only until the tab closes.
